name: Rian Gauvreau
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Clio; Founder & CEO, Aeon Health (Vancouver)
profile: Vancouver entrepreneur who co-founded legal-practice-management SaaS Clio with Jack Newton in 2008; served as COO until 2017, then chief people officer until stepping back in 2021, staying on the board. In 2023 he founded Aeon Health, an AI-focused health-tech company, aiming to do for health care what Clio did for law.
interesting_fact: Before Clio he worked as a legal technologist at a Vancouver law firm, where he and Newton concluded that existing practice software was clunky and expensive; Clio became the first-to-market cloud practice-management product.
deep_cut_fact: He and Clio co-founder Jack Newton are lifelong friends whose first joint 'venture' dates back to Grade 3. He also earned his UBC Sauder MBA ('11) while growing Clio, and in 2025 became the first Sauder grad to win UBC's Alumni Achievement Award for Entrepreneurship.
notes: Aeon Health site lists only support@/work@ inboxes; best route likely via Aeon Health or Clio comms. Departure dates from Clio ops differ by source (2019 vs 2021).

name: Elad Raz
profile: Israeli chip entrepreneur who founded NextSilicon in 2017 to build adaptive 'Maverick' processors for HPC and AI as an alternative to GPUs. Earlier he founded Integrity Project, a low-level software/security firm acquired by Mellanox in 2014, and then served as a software director at Mellanox. NextSilicon has raised ~$300M and has 400+ staff.
interesting_fact: His first company, Integrity Project (founded 2006, Ramat Gan), was formed out of an elite military technology unit and was bought by Mellanox in July 2014 for its software expertise.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong retro-computing fan: he got hooked tinkering with Commodore 64s and Ataris as a kid and says he still collects them to this day.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI-compute theme. info@ is the company's general inbox. Writes a blog on nextsilicon.com/insights.

name: Sandeep K Gupta
profile: Co-founder of Innovaccer, the San Francisco-based healthcare data platform (India's first health-tech unicorn, valued ~$3-4B). An engineer with an MBA in finance from IIM Ahmedabad, he ran operations and is credited with helping drive ~100% revenue CAGR; he now serves as President.
interesting_fact: Innovaccer grew out of a Wharton/Harvard data-analytics research project on combining distributed datasets; Gupta met co-founder Abhinav Shashank while both worked at Ingersoll Rand.
notes: Common name; identified via Innovaccer leadership page. Low personal public profile.

name: Matt Kennedy
profile: Listed as a co-founder of Public.com, the New York investing app co-founded with Jannick Malling, Leif Abraham and Sean Hendelman, where he led brokerage operations and served as COO. Public is valued at over $1B. Details come mainly from directory profiles; current title unverified.
interesting_fact: Before Public he reportedly worked as a trading associate at broker-dealer Dominick & Dominick (per a company-profile listing).
notes: Very common name and low profile; only aggregator sources confirm role. Public's media contact is Rachel Livingston (press@public.com).

name: Yada Piyajomkwan
profile: Thai-born co-founder of Jakarta online brokerage Ajaib, started in 2019 with Stanford GSB classmate Anderson Sumarli; it became a unicorn in 2021 and passed one million investors. Ex-McKinsey and Unilever, Stanford MBA '19; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.
interesting_fact: Ajaib went through Y Combinator and hit a $1B valuation in 2021 only about two years after founding; Stanford GSB later wrote a teaching case on it.
deep_cut_fact: She mentors women through UNHCR's Leading Women Fund and She Loves Tech, and was profiled by UNHCR Thailand for that work.
notes: Some older sources list her as COO; recent ones say CPO.

name: Andrew Barnes
current_role: Co-founder & director, Go1 (stepped down as co-CEO Aug 2024)
profile: Brisbane entrepreneur who co-founded workplace-learning platform Go1 with high-school friends Vu Tran, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; it went through Y Combinator and reached a ~$3B valuation. He led it as CEO for about a decade before handing the top job to Eigeland in 2024.
interesting_fact: Go1 started in a Brisbane suburban garage as a web-development shop he ran with Vu Tran; it now serves 10,000+ organisations and 50M+ users.
deep_cut_fact: A 2013 Rhodes Scholar, he did an Oxford MSc in Education (Learning and Technology) and a UQ PhD in business management, after UQ degrees in economics (2009) and business management honours (2011).
notes: Common name - distinguish from the NZ 4-day-week Andrew Barnes. Holds a doctorate (Dr Andrew Barnes).

name: Hovhannes Avoyan
profile: Armenian-American serial entrepreneur (b. 1965, Yerevan) who co-founded photo/video editor Picsart in 2011 and built it into a 150M+ MAU creative platform. Earlier companies (CEDIT, Sourcio, Monitis and others) were sold to buyers including Lycos, GFI/TeamViewer and HelpSystems.
interesting_fact: Five of his startups before Picsart were acquired by global companies, and he was founding president of Armenia's Union of IT Enterprises (2000-2015).
deep_cut_fact: Besides a 1987 computer science degree, he holds a master's in political science and international affairs from the American University of Armenia (1995), which gave him its Distinguished Alumni Award in 2016; he also sits on AUA's board of trustees.
notes: Active speaker/writer on AI; has a TechCrunch contributor page.

name: Tessa Wijaya
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Xendit (also reported as CEO of Xendit Thailand)
profile: Indonesian co-founder and COO of Xendit, the Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company (Y Combinator alum, valued ~$3B). A former private-equity analyst, she oversees operations, partnerships, compliance and government relations, and is often cited as Indonesia's first female unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: She joined Xendit in 2016 after being introduced via Y Combinator to the UC Berkeley founders working on payments, having spotted the missing payment rails while working with early-stage startups in private equity.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in a small Indonesian town raised by her grandmother, who ran a small food business, and landed her first PE analyst job in Jakarta with no finance background, teaching herself finance on her own time.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference speaker. Xendit press releases have named Ami Windarti (PR & Comms) as media contact; I could not verify the address directly.

name: Gustavo Chamati
profile: Brazilian entrepreneur who co-founded Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, with his brother Mauricio in 2013. It became the base of holding group 2TM, Brazil's first crypto unicorn after SoftBank invested $200M in 2021. Formerly CEO, he now sits on the board.
interesting_fact: 2TM grew beyond the exchange into a group including digital bank MeuBank, custody firm Bitrust, Blockchain Academy and others, though Mercado Bitcoin still drove 90%+ of revenue.
notes: Sources disagree on whether he is still CEO or only board member. Best route likely Mercado Bitcoin press office.

name: Jack Pierse
current_role: Co-founder & former CFO, Wayflyer; angel investor
profile: Irish chartered accountant who co-founded Dublin e-commerce revenue-based financing company Wayflyer with Aidan Corbett in 2019 and served as CFO; it hit unicorn status in ~29 months. He stepped away in 2023 to pursue new ventures and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: Aidan Corbett credits Pierse with coming up with the original idea for Wayflyer in 2019; he saw the working-capital squeeze first-hand while working at an e-commerce accelerator.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he joined the $20M Series A of US fintech startup Arc as an angel investor.
notes: No public contact found; post-Wayflyer venture not confirmed.

name: Nick Humphreys
profile: Melbourne designer who co-founded Linktree in 2016 with brothers Alex and Anthony Zaccaria out of their music/entertainment digital agency Bolster, after tiring of constantly updating clients' single bio link. Linktree grew into a $1.3B 'link in bio' platform; he leads design and creative direction.
interesting_fact: Linktree started as an internal fix at Bolster in Collingwood, where the team kept rewriting artists' single social-media bio link.
deep_cut_fact: He spent four years in London designing for brands including Barclays and Manchester United, calls himself a 'brutalist design evangelist', and has two Webby nominations.

name: Maximiliano Casal
current_role: Co-founder & former COO, Nowports; building a new AI company
profile: Uruguayan systems engineer (Universidad ORT) and ex-iOS developer who co-founded digital freight forwarder Nowports with Mexico's Alfonso de los Rios in 2018; it went through YC and became a unicorn after a $150M Series C in 2022. He later left the COO role and is building a new AI-related company.
interesting_fact: He met co-founder Alfonso de los Rios at a Stanford-run software development seminar in 2017; Nowports made him only the third Uruguayan unicorn founder after dLocal's founders.
deep_cut_fact: Before logistics he was a hands-on mobile engineer: senior iOS developer and team lead at Moove-it, iOS developer at Globant, and co-founder/CTO of Croway.

name: Sebastián Noguera Escallón
profile: Colombian entrepreneur who co-founded Bogota proptech Habi with CEO Brynne McNulty around 2019; it buys and sells homes for Latin America's middle class and became Colombia's second unicorn. Earlier he was Chief Digital Officer at Banco de Bogota and co-founded online grocer Merqueo.
interesting_fact: Habi uses data to give quick offers on middle-class apartments in Colombia and Mexico; he argues Latin Americans invest in apartments rather than the stock market.
deep_cut_fact: Before Habi he led the digital transformation of Banco de Bogota as its Chief Digital Officer, and he co-founded Merqueo, which became Colombia's largest digital supermarket.

name: Tanuj Gulati
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Securonix; part of Austin FC ownership group
profile: Cybersecurity entrepreneur and investor. A founding member of identity-governance firm Vaau (sold to Sun Microsystems), he co-founded SIEM company Securonix with Sachin Nayyar and served as CTO, growing ARR past $100M. Nayyar also founded Saviynt; I found no primary source naming Gulati as a Saviynt co-founder.
interesting_fact: He is part of the ownership group of MLS club Austin FC; a lifelong soccer fan, he played varsity soccer at school and still plays.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BS in computer applications and an MBA from Oklahoma State University, and serves on the boards of the Miracle Foundation and Austin Speech Labs.
notes: Hurun lists him under Saviynt; documented roles are Vaau, Oracle/Sun, Securonix. Verify the Saviynt link before outreach.

name: Matt Pfeil
current_role: Co-founder, DataStax; advisor/EIR (Top Tier Capital Partners, per profiles)
profile: Co-founded Apache Cassandra company DataStax (originally Riptano, Austin) with Jonathan Ellis in 2010 after both left Rackspace; he served as VP Customer Solutions and Chief Customer Officer to 2017. DataStax was acquired by IBM in 2025; he has since advised and invested in startups.
interesting_fact: Rackspace gave the founders just under $100,000 in seed money as a note when they spun out to commercialise Cassandra.
deep_cut_fact: A Virginia Tech CS grad, he started in infrastructure at Blacksburg email-hosting startup Webmail.us, then built and ran Rackspace's Email and Apps infrastructure development group.
notes: Current roles come from aggregator profiles. Relevant to data/data-center theme.

name: Guy Teverovsky
profile: Israeli identity-security engineer who co-founded Semperis (Hoboken NJ / Tel Aviv) with Mickey Bresman and Matan Liberman around 2013-2015; it makes Active Directory and hybrid identity protection and recovery tools and is valued at $1B+. He leads R&D.
interesting_fact: Semperis was accepted into Microsoft's accelerator program early on, and the co-founders recruited him from Microsoft.
deep_cut_fact: Before Semperis he spent five years as a Senior Premier Field Engineer at Microsoft specialising in Active Directory for EMEA enterprises, and was named a Microsoft Directory Services MVP.
notes: billk@ is Semperis' published PR contact (Bill Keeler). Appeared on SC Media 'Founder Stories' podcast.

name: Remington Tonar
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Growth Officer, Cart.com; Adjunct Professor, Rice Business
profile: Houston entrepreneur who co-founded commerce and logistics company Cart.com with Omair Tariq in 2020, serving as CFO, COO, CRO and CGO and leading Cart Government Solutions. Earlier he ran Houston incubator The Cannon and co-managed a seed venture fund; he is a GP at Flyleaf Capital and teaches at Rice.
interesting_fact: He holds a PhD from the University of Aberdeen on AI and society and wrote 'AI Theism: Technology, Divinity, and the Emergence of a New Religious Myth' (Routledge, 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He used to be a senior contributor to Forbes.com, writing about infrastructure innovation and smart cities, after years in corporate innovation consulting in New York.
notes: Frequent speaker (SXSW, Web Summit, Shoptalk); writes on cart.com blog.

name: He Jian
current_role: President, Dongchedi (DCar), ByteDance's auto platform (as of 2020)
profile: Likely He Jian (He Jian, Chinese 何戬), president of Dongchedi (DCar), the car-information and auto-commerce app spun out of Toutiao's auto channel in 2017. ByteDance reportedly sought ~$700-800M for DCar at a ~$3B valuation in 2024. Little public biography exists.
interesting_fact: At DCar's 2020 creator conference he said the platform became China's largest auto livestreaming platform just 10 months after launching livestreams in October 2019.
notes: Name in list may refer to 何戬 (DCar president); 'founder' label unverified - DCar is a ByteDance product. Keep outreach minimal; route via ByteDance/DCar PR.

name: David Goldin
profile: Fintech pioneer who founded AmeriMerchant in 2002, one of the first US merchant cash advance companies, expanding to the UK and Australia in 2008; the brands were unified as Capify in 2015 and the US arm was sold to focus on UK/Australian SME lending, backed by Goldman Sachs credit facilities.
interesting_fact: He started in fintech 'before the word fintech was even coined', launching one of the first MCA companies in the early 2000s.
deep_cut_fact: He was a founding member and president of the North American Merchant Advance Association, now the Small Business Financing Association, the industry's trade body.

name: Sami Jenkins
profile: Co-founder and COO of Orlando-based Zero Trust endpoint security company ThreatLocker, launched in 2017 with Danny Jenkins and John Carolan. With ~20 years in IT starting in tech support and sysadmin work, she oversees operations, product, engineering, sales and support and global expansion.
interesting_fact: She led ThreatLocker through an 83% headcount increase in 2024; its 'Cyber Hero' support team answers requests in about a minute on average.
deep_cut_fact: Before ThreatLocker she co-founded email-security developer Sirrustec and founded PRD Technology, an IT management and software services firm; she was a finalist in CRN's inaugural Women of the Year awards (2023).
